documents.text: Jira issues are considered overdue when their due date has passed.
A sprint is a fixed period during which a team works on planned issues.
A Jira board displays issues and their current workflow status.
GitHub pull requests are used to review code before merging.
Jira provides native support for complex Scrum and Kanban boards.
Developers can advance a Jira issue status (e.g., from 'In Progress' to 'Done') simply by typing the issue key and a command (like PROJ-123 #comment done) inside a GitHub commit message.
Project managers, QA testers, and stakeholders can view branches, commit histories, and pull request statuses directly inside Jira without needing a GitHub license.
Jira uses the synced GitHub data to calculate exact cycle times, deployment frequencies, and release readiness metrics on its built-in DevOps dashboards.
The integration tracks code deployments through GitHub Actions, allowing Jira to display exactly which environment (like Staging or Production) a specific feature is live on.
Advanced configurations let GitHub Advanced Security push vulnerability alerts directly into Jira as high-priority bugs, ensuring developers patch security flaws quickly.
